validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE / CLASSIFICATION / STATUS / FUEL confirmed by multiple independent, non-GEM origins spanning 1996-2026. This is a real, currently-operating Louisiana intrastate natural gas transportation and storage network correctly classified as gas (not NGL/oil): (1) a 1996 Federal Register notice (govinfo.gov, an offshore-gathering-line certificate proceeding) references existing facilities of 'Bridgeline Gas Distribution LLC' near Larose, Lafourche Parish, Louisiana -- a government document wholly independent of GEM/the company, predating even the 2000 restructuring; (2) contemporaneous 2000 press coverage (New York Times, Natural Gas Intelligence) reports Texaco and Enron combining their SE-Louisiana intrastate pipeline and storage assets, effective March 1 2000, into the joint venture 'Bridgeline Holdings, L.P.'; (3) a chain of ownership-transaction press/SEC sources (Targa Resources 2004 press release + 2011 SEC Form 424B1 prospectus, both independent of GEM, describing Targa's $101M purchase of a 40% interest from the Enron bankruptcy estate and Chevron's $117M buyback of that stake in 2005) confirms continuous real operation through the 2000s; (4) EnLink Midstream's 2014 acquisition of Chevron's Gulf Coast gas pipeline systems (Oil & Gas Journal / World Pipelines trade-press coverage, worldpipelines.com verified live) explicitly lists 'Bridgeline System: approximately 985 miles of natural gas pipelines in Southern Louisiana with a total system capacity of approximately 920,000 [thousand cf/d, i.e. 920 MMcf/d]' -- both GEM figures (LengthKnown=1585.00 km = 985.0 mi exactly; Capacity=920.00 MMcf/d) match this named, dated, on-the-record transaction description; (5) the operator's own current page (oneok.com/bridgeline, verified live, names 'Bridgeline Holdings, L.P.') and ONEOK's FY2025 Form 10-K Exhibit 21 (SEC EDGAR, verified live) both confirm the entity is live and operating today as an intrastate gas pipeline/storage system in Louisiana. Classification (natural-gas transmission/distribution network, not gathering-only, not NGL) is consistent across every source -- FERC's 1996 filing even distinguishes the OFFSHORE gathering line under discussion FROM Bridgeline's onshore distribution facilities, i.e. an independent regulator drawing exactly the classification line GEM draws. DUPLICATE CHECK against the 50-row Gulf-Coast roster: no other row matches this system -- Acadian, Louisiana Intrastate Gas (LIG), Regency Intrastate Gas (RIGS), and Tiger are distinct, separately-owned Louisiana intrastate networks per every source read; no merge/relabel indicated. CROSS-ROW LEAD: the same 2014 EnLink/Chevron transaction description also states figures for the 'Chandeleur System' that match roster row P0165 almost exactly -- see cross_row_leads. CITATION POOL: 10 citations harvested from this wiki page; opened/checked 6 (bridgeline.enlink.com about page -- live plus a 2022 Wayback capture with a fuller spec table; worldpipelines.com EnLink-acquisition article -- live, the key 985-mi/920-MMcf/d source; nytimes.com 2000 Texaco/Enron piece -- live via Wayback, original nytimes.com 403s scripted clients; SEC 424B1 Targa prospectus -- live; ogj.com EnLink-purchase article -- live but JS-rendered, title/metadata confirmed, full prose not extractable). 4 were access failures, not deletions, so none were dropped: businesswire.com 2014 EnLink release (ReadTimeout, no Wayback capture found -- its content is duplicated by the worldpipelines/ogj coverage already used); ir.targaresources.com 2004 press-release page (ReadTimeout, no Wayback capture, but the same $101M/40% fact is independently in the SEC 424B1 and corroborated by a targaresources.com static-file release found via search); bizjournals.com 2005 Chevron piece (HTTP 403, no Wayback capture); wsj.com Henry Hub feature (HTTP 401 paywall, general Henry Hub context, does not appear to name Bridgeline specifically so not essential). The 10th citation (bit.ly/2rA4ZOp, an A Barrel Full / abarrelfull.wikidot.com redirect) was intentionally NOT opened or used -- banned source, standing rule 5.

validity.researcher_notes: TWO CAVEATS worth flagging even though no sheet value changes: (1) StartYear1=2000 is well-documented as the year Texaco and Enron's combined Louisiana system began operating AS 'Bridgeline Holdings, L.P.' (NYT + Natural Gas Intelligence, both contemporaneous Feb 2000, independent of each other) -- but a 1996 Federal Register notice already references facilities of 'Bridgeline Gas Distribution LLC' at the same Larose location, meaning some of the underlying physical pipe predates the 2000 joint-venture formation by at least 4 years, likely built by Texaco or a predecessor over prior decades. 2000 is defensible as 'when Bridgeline as a unified entity began operating' but is not a construction date for the whole network -- consistent with ConstructionYear being blank/unresolved (see fills) rather than fabricating an earlier figure I can't pin down. (2) Length (1585.00 km = 985.0 mi) and Capacity (920.00 MMcf/d) are corroborated verbatim by ONE strong, dated, on-the-record source (the September 2014 EnLink/Chevron Gulf Coast asset-purchase description, reported identically by Business Wire, Oil & Gas Journal, and World Pipelines -- all tracing to the same underlying transaction disclosure, so treated as ONE origin per the wire-story rule, not three). I searched for a second, genuinely independent origin (Rextag -- no Bridgeline page found; PHMSA/NPMS -- not fetchable in this pass; EIA pipeline-projects tables -- not checked for this system specifically) and could not find one giving the same precision. The company's own current/2022 self-description ('more than 1,000 miles' / '1,030 miles') is directionally consistent (985-1,030 mi is a plausible range for a system with minor incremental laterals added over a decade) but is not precise enough to count as a clean second confirmation of 985.0 mi exactly. Tier is therefore MEDIUM, not high, on Length/Capacity -- see the paired fills entries.
